sense: a train’s puffing, in children’s talk

evidence: Verg. A. 8.421 (Lewis & Short s.v. anhēlō): fornācibus ignis anhēlat
terms.comment: No ancient form of the sound is known, and trains are modern. The classical verb for panting, which Vergil uses of the fire in the Cyclopes’ furnaces, applied by us to the puffs of a steam engine.

terms.gloss: whistle, hiss (of the train’s whistle and steam)
evidence: Ov. Met. 12.279 (Lewis & Short s.v. sībilō): of red-hot iron hissing in water
terms.comment: The classical verb for a hiss or a whistle, applied by us to the train.

phrases.english: Do you hear the train puffing?

sources: Lewis & Short: anhelo · Lewis & Short: sibilo
No ancient form of the sound is known; the uses are ours, on the classical verbs.
